prelude: A receiver listens to the Dribel telegraph line. Encoding: the sender repeats a single bit 5 times. The Dribel telegraph line is noisy with probability 37 percent (and quiet otherwise) for the whole transmission; each bit is flipped independently with probability 5 percent when quiet and 28 percent when noisy. The message is 0 with probability 29 percent and 1 with probability 71 percent. Later, position 4 will be retransmitted once more over the same line, in the same (quiet or noisy) condition; the retransmission is acknowledged and resent until it arrives, so it is never erased, but it can still be flipped like any other bit.
